analysis_sections.text: The transformed view retains the outline of the speaking face and parts of the mouth and eyes, while replacing fine appearance with a coarse banded structure. Comparing it to the original crop helps distinguish visible expression from the effect of graph filtering. It supplies an alternative structural perspective on this portrait, while the signed readouts and region tests answer the separate question of how model outputs respond.
analysis_sections.title: A transformed view of the same face

analysis_sections.text: The middle and final displayed pairs place prominent positive readouts along the far viewer-right grid column. Earlier views can emphasize different lower-central cells. This is important to retain rather than turning every heatmap into a nose or mouth explanation. Contribution shows signed support at the classifier readout; the spatial pattern is specific to the sampled pair and need not coincide with the compact attention proposal.
analysis_sections.title: Where the classifier readout supports its decision

analysis_sections.text: The separate explanation head proposes a central facial focus, with a connected region covering part of the eye and nose area. That proposal differs from the strongest outer-grid contributions. Unsigned attention measures learned importance for organizing an explanation, not a calibrated fake probability or the classifier’s internal attention coefficients. Reading the views together shows the distinction between classifier support and a compact region suggested for inspection.
analysis_sections.title: The explanation head’s proposed focus

analysis_sections.text: The saved whole-curve comparisons do not favor the central candidate over the strongest matched controls. Some endpoint responses are positive or favorable, but they do not establish the full regional criterion. The selected region is therefore presented as an observational model-focus proposal. The strong video-level assessment and pair-specific signed contributions remain available to explain the overall direction of the prediction.

inherited_editor_changes.after:
A blonde woman speaks in a close studio portrait with a dark background. Across the short windows, her lips move from a slight smile to more rounded and closed shapes while her head and gaze shift subtly. The clear facial framing makes it possible to compare visible expression with the source-aligned contribution, attention and spectral views.

SSTGNN strongly favors manipulated. The signed contribution pattern changes across pairs, with strong positive support along the viewer-right grid edge in the middle and final displayed views. Learned attention selects a more central facial region. These distinct emphases reveal complementary model views, while the recorded controls do not qualify the central candidate as a local explanation.
inherited_editor_changes.before: The video shows a speaker with blonde hair in a studio setting, delivering speech with natural mouth movements and consistent gaze across sparse original frames and two short consecutive sequences. The detector assigns an extremely high calibrated fake score, indicating strong evidence of manipulation despite the visually coherent appearance. The explanation maps reveal a concentrated attention region over the face center, but the strongest positive classifier contributions arise from viewer-right facial zones, not the nose or upper lip.
